questions.question: What is the difference between IQueryable, IEnumerable and List in C#, and when do you use each?
questions.shortAnswer: `IEnumerable<T>` … Filtering: Happens in memory after the data is loaded. … `IQueryable<T>` … Filtering: Happens at the data source (e.g., SQL WHERE clause). … `List<T>` … Deferred Execution: No — data is already loaded.

answerFrom.section: # Here’s a clear, practical breakdown of IQueryable, IEnumerable, and List in C#, along with when to use each.

code.source:
IQueryable<User> users = dbContext.Users; // From EF DbSet
var activeUsers = users.Where(u => u.IsActive); // Translates to SQL WHERE

questions.question: What is the N+1 problem, and how do you fix it?
questions.shortAnswer: The N+1 problem occurs when an application executes one query to fetch data and then N additional queries to fetch related data, leading to performance issues. … Eager Loading (Best Solution)
